For the past few weeks, my favorite spot has been BXVL Coffeehouse in Bronxville, New York. I had been there a few times before and always thought of it as just a place to stop while waiting for a train. However, as the weather in Bronxville has warmed and I’ve ventured out of my cozy house more often, I’ve really come to enjoy spending time at this coffeehouse with friends and my boyfriend.

The matcha is fresh and delicious, but my personal go-to—an iced black tea with honey—is amazing and might just be turning into a new addiction. Their ready-to-go sandwiches are also fresh and flavorful. Last time I was there, I had the caprese sandwich, which tasted like a deliciously fresh bite straight from a garden. My boyfriend had a sandwich with turkey, tomatoes, lettuce, banana peppers, and mayo, which was also fresh and tasty.

Overall, this place has such a great vibe, with a cozy interior that almost makes me feel like I’m in a library. It’s a perfect way to start the day and a spot I’d highly recommend to anyone in the area.

📍Antonio’s Trattoria - 2370 Belmont Avenue - Bronx, NY

Antonio’s Trattoria is an Italian restaurant that opened in the Bronx’s “Little Italy” in 2006. The restaurant was founded by owner Anthony Lancione and his two business partners. The three friends grew up near Arthur Avenue and saw the need for an establishment that brought diners back to the old world in way of food and atmosphere. The trattoria serves everything from Italian-American classics like Chicken Parmigiana to house-made pasta dishes to thin crust pizza. They also boast an extensive wine selection.

My family and I recently had dinner at Antonio’s after spending the day at the nearby Bronx Zoo. This was our third visit to the restaurant. We thought it would be fun to get dinner in Little Italy afterwards. My wife, son and I have been to Antonio’s before and thought that my parents would enjoy it too. We made a reservation for early evening. For drinks, I ordered a glass of Montepulciano while my wife enjoyed a glass of white sangria. For food, I ordered the “Salmon Dijon” (served w/ escarole in a dijon mustard sauce with polenta) with a side of garlic-sautéed broccoli, my wife had the “Endive & Gorgonzola Salad” (endive, walnuts, apples, gorgonzola cheese, roasted peppers, EVOO & balsamic vinegar) with grilled chicken added, and our sons had “Ravioli with Tomato Sauce” and “Spaghetti & Meatball” off the Kid’s menu. Afterwards, we ordered plates of “Cannoli” (fresh-filled to order; courtesy of Artuso’s Pastry Shop down the street) for our sons to enjoy. They were very pleased! Another fantastic experience at Antonio’s! We hope to come back again and again! 🇮🇹
I’m a regular here btw 🤭

When in the Bronx, a stop at Antonio’s Trattoria is a must. For me, it’s become a tradition to indulge here after a visit to the New York Botanical Garden! 🌸🌳

Delicious doesn’t even begin to cover it. The eggplant rollatini? Absolutely spectacular. The salad pizza? Crisp, fresh, and bursting with flavor. But the true star of the show… their mouthwatering garlic knots — simply divine. 😋🤩❤️

Antonio’s delivers top-notch Italian favorites with warm, attentive service to match. Be sure to save this spot — or better yet, join me, and I’ll make sure you order all the right things. 🍝

The “Breaking Bread Building Bonds” initiative, launched by the New York City Mayor’s Office represents a bold commitment to fostering community unity and combating hate crimes. This initiative emphasizes the value of diversity, experiences, and histories within our neighborhoods, believing this understanding enhances relationships among residents. 

By fostering appreciation for diversity, individuals can cultivate empathy and connections, highlighting our shared humanity. Celebrating diversity also strengthens belonging and leads to more positive interactions, creating a unified, resilient community.

On November 13, 2024, the Breaking Bread initiative came to light as community members gathered in a warm and welcoming atmosphere at Antonio's Trattoria @antoniostrattoria , hosted by the NYPD’s 48th Precinct. This gathering provided a platform for community members from diverse backgrounds to unite over dinner, engaging in lively conversations and exchanging stories and ideas. This inviting setting, allowed community leaders and NYPD Community Affairs established meaningful connections, strengthening the spirit of togetherness that is vital for a flourishing community.

First is the veal sorrentino with eggplant and mozzarella and a white wine & butter sauce which was actually totally the move and i made a mistake by not ordering that. Next is the veal saltimbocca which is veal with prosciutto de parma, spinach, and mozzarella in a marsala wine sauce. We got the garlic bread with mozzarella (straight from casa della mozzarella sooo soo good) and that was actually the best garlic bread ive ever had. 10/10 every time order the veal here you can cut it with a fork or the pizza but make sure the mozzarella is from casa della mozzarella or else its not worth it.

Did you know that Sunday is Happy Hour all day long at the bar? We didn’t either — but what a find! With $1 Blue Point oysters, discounted appetizers, and reduced prices on cocktails, wine, and beer, it was impossible to say no.

What began as a casual stop for a drink at the bar turned into a full-blown, delightfully unexpected birthday celebration at @ZeroOttoNove. Tucked away like a hidden gem, this place quickly became the highlight of my day — and honestly, one of the best spontaneous lunches I’ve had in a long time.

The Blue Point oysters 🦪 were an absolute standout. Some of the plumpest, sweetest, and largest oysters I’ve had in years — and at just $1 each? Truly unbelievable. 

For my main dish, I went with the Risotto con Ragù Bianco, and it was a great choice. The creamy Arborio rice was perfectly cooked and sautéed with shredded short rib, green peas, yellow beets, Parmigiano, and a bit of peppercorn for depth. The flavor had a wonderful essence of black truffle 🍄‍🟫 — subtle but present — that added a rich, earthy note without overpowering the dish. 

My husband had the Orecchiette con Broccoli Rabe. It was a simple, flavorful dish with broccoli rabe that had just the right bite from spicy pecorino.

We finished by sharing the Sogni Cioccolato — layers of chocolate cake and dark chocolate mousse with a touch of Grand Marnier, all encased in a smooth Nutella ganache shell. Rich and satisfying.

The service was excellent — friendly, attentive, and professional. And the ambiance was just what we were looking for: upscale but relaxed, great for a special occasion or a leisurely Sunday afternoon.

Zero Otto Nove has several locations — not just here, but also in Armonk, NYC, and the Bronx — so no matter where you are, you’re not too far from a great meal.

The Jewish Museum’s Warburg Mansion is among the 200 New York City landmark replicas recreated from bark and leaves at the annual New York Botanical Garden Holiday Train Show, on view through January 11, 2026. Built in 1908 as the family home of Felix and Frieda Warburg, the building is an example of the homes that once adorned “millionaire’s row” on Fifth Avenue during the Gilded Age, like Andrew Carnegie (now @CooperHewitt) and William K. Vanderbilt.

The Warburgs made their home the center of activities of vital importance to them: philanthropy, the collection and care of art, and the stewardship of Jewish culture. In keeping with these interests, the family later donated the building to the Jewish Theological Seminary for use as a museum, and its doors opened to the public as the Jewish Museum in 1947.

Frankie’s Restaurant. Arthur Avenue and E 186th Street. What to say about Frankie’s? It’s a classic kind of old-school, red-sauce, Italian-American, howyoudoin-fugedabowdit, kind of place. It was completely empty when I went for lunch, (to be expected at 1pm on a weekday). The menu isn’t massive, which I like, featuring all the typical Italian dishes you would expect in a place like this. My waitress was quick and nice, she recommended Chicken alla Vodka which came with penne. I can’t complain about the food at all, it was very much solid. I took a peak at the cocktail menu and I wasn’t impressed, (muddling a cherry and orange in an old fashioned?? In 2025??). I went with a glass of house red, which was very much serviceable. The food was $33 and the wine was $15, definitely on the pricey side but not completely outrageous. All in all, I’d give Frankie’s an 8.6/10. It’s not somewhere I’d cross two Burroughs to get to, but if you’re in the area and want a pretty good Italian place, Frankie’s is your spot.

caption:
Everyday Happy Hour, great drinks, some awesome codfish fritters, and Rasta pasta with oxtail. That’s naming just a few things I sampled at @flavabx, and if you were to lock me up inside this restaurant and then you threw away the key I’d be perfectly okay with that. 

I feel like if you’re not from the Bronx or haven’t educated yourself enough on the diversity of the borough then you’d never know of the myriad Caribbean food options in the Boogie Down. Maybe an outsider could surmise that the BX offers up some great Dominican/Puerto Rican food or old school Italian food. But would they know about the many Jamaican spots scattered across? It’s a true, real life case of IYKYK aka Only The Real Ones. 

All the other boroughs (except for Staten Island… cause ain’t nobody go there) get celebrated for their cuisines and popular restaurants. And while it’s taken much longer for the northernmost borough to get its time in the culinary spotlight, I’ve no doubt it’ll continue to shine as brightly as the others do - and perhaps even brighter. #TheHungryDominican 🇩🇴

Royal 35 Steakhouse takes pride in dry-aging its steaks in-house for 30–35 days, and you can actually see the cuts on display in their glass aging locker as you walk in. I ordered the New York Strip, medium rare, with mashed potatoes on the side. I didn’t realize it was bone-in, but that turned out to be a great surprise.

The steak arrived sizzling hot, carved off the bone and served in thick slices. It was well over an inch thick, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor—tender, juicy, and rich from the dry-aging process. Normally, I’m a ribeye person, but this strip was outstanding and easily over 20 ounces. The mashed potatoes were smooth and buttery, a great complement to the steak.

The service was excellent—attentive without being overbearing—and really added to the experience. Overall, Royal 35 delivered on both quality and atmosphere. I’d give it 4.5 stars and definitely plan on returning.
